description.prosthetics: We provide free, high-quality prosthetics for soldiers and civilians who have lost limbs due to the war.
description.rehabilitation: We offer comprehensive rehabilitation in the US alongside dedicated mental health support in Ukraine.
description.expertise: Our expertise lies in pediatric prosthetics and complex clinical cases.

cards.description: Direct Relief has been our key and trusted partner for many years. Working side by side with us, the organization helps carry out our most critical initiatives and supports our projects at every stage. Thank you for your unwavering faith in our mission, your steadfast support, and our shared work to improve the lives of Ukrainians!

Protez Foundation CEO and co-founder Yura Aroshidze with Keith Kellogg, the U.S. Special Envoy for Ukraine and former National Security Advisor to the U.S. Vice President, during a meeting in Washington. We expressed our gratitude for the consistent and unwavering support for Ukraine.

Since 2022, we have had the honor of working side by side with the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine on vital projects: providing prosthetic care, training specialists, organizing specialized educational programs in the United States for lyceum students whose parents were killed or went missing while defending Ukraine, and supporting and equipping State Emergency Service units responding to the aftermath of enemy attacks. We are grateful to our partners for our shared values, which place people and work that delivers results at the heart of everything we do.

A meeting with a German government delegation led by Parliamentary State Secretary Johann Saathoff to discuss strengthening Ukraine’s healthcare system. In appreciation of Germany’s sustained support for Ukraine, Protez Foundation co-founder Yura Aroshidze presented Mr. Saathoff with a commemorative coin.

Protez Foundation and the patronage service of the Khartiia 2nd Corps of the National Guard of Ukraine signed a memorandum of cooperation to provide comprehensive readjustment support and ongoing assistance to wounded service members and veterans. We are already carrying out joint initiatives, including a major conference for 250 support service specialists from different regions.
Protez Foundation Chief Medical Director and co-founder Yakov Gradinar receives an award from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

A memorandum on the continuation of cooperation between the Protez Foundation and the Ministry of Health of Ukraine has been signed. Our goal is unity in support and assistance to our heroes who deserve the best. Together we can achieve significant changes in prosthetic care and the provision of high-quality prostheses.

Collaboration and unity are the key to success in our common desire to provide prosthetics and rehabilitation of our heroes at a high level. We have extended the memorandum of cooperation with the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine and successfully implement joint projects for training specialists and prosthetics for military personnel.
Direct Relief – our reliable partner who inspires us with their mission to help people around the world. Their support in achieving the goals of the Prosthetics Foundation in Ukraine is invaluable.

prostheticsForUkrainians.description1: Since the start of the full-scale invasion, we have been working consistently to restore freedom of movement and improve the quality of life for Ukrainians who have lost limbs as a result of the war. By providing high-quality prosthetic care in Ukraine and the US, we help patients regain their physical independence.

description: High-quality prosthetic care is a complex and costly process that requires advanced materials and the expertise of skilled specialists. For Ukrainians who have lost limbs as a result of the war, all services and prostheses provided through our program are completely free of charge.

This is made possible by the ongoing support of our donors, financial partners, and everyday contributions from people who care. We use every contribution responsibly: we optimize logistics, work with leading manufacturers, and minimize operating expenses so that as much of the funding as possible goes directly toward helping patients.

items.name: Vadym
items.title: Vadym has dedicated 10 years to the Ukrainian Army.
items.text: Defending Ukraine, he lost two legs with high amputations. Vadym is motivated and does not give up, he inspires everyone with his example. Vadym is currently in the USA undergoing prosthetics fitting and rehabilitation.  Only with your help we are able to fit Vadym with modern bionic prosthetics and return him to a full life. Together we are united and strong. Thank you for sharing this post and for your donations

items.name: Artem
items.title: Artem played for the Mariupol youth soccer club, and he wanted to be a professional soccer player.
items.text: Artem’s dream was to dedicate his life to soccer.  On March 2nd, 2022, he went to the local field to play a scrimmage match with his friends. While they were warming up, a Russian drone dropped a grenade on the field. Artem’s best friend Ilya, a boy of 15, was killed. Artem and another boy were severely injured. As a result of the injuries, Artem’s left leg was amputated above the knee, and his right leg is paralyzed. Artem’s dream is now to be able to walk again.

items.name: Volodymyr
items.title: His dream is to run, jump and play football...
items.text: Volodya, a 10-year-old boy from the Dnipropetrovsk region, was born with atrophied lower limbs and spent years moving on his hands and knees. After the amputation of both lower limbs, he traveled to Minneapolis with the support of the Protez Foundation and took his first steps on training prosthetics. His determination and joy were incredible, as he was able to walk proudly for the first time in his life.

releases.title: Prosthetic and Rehabilitation Center based on the Ministry of Internal Affairs: an important initiative for military personnel
releases.text: On December 12, a meeting was held at the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine with the Minister of Internal Affairs Ihor Klymenko, the General Director of the Protez Foundation Yura Aroshidze, and the President of Direct Relief Thomas Tighe. The meeting was also attended by Deputy Minister of Internal Affairs of Ukraine Kateryna Pavlichenko. The main topic of negotiations was the creation of a prosthetic and rehabilitation center based on one of the medical institutions of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

releases.title: Training of the Protez Foundation team in the USA
releases.text: The Ukrainian team of the Protez Foundation has successfully completed its two-week stay in the USA! 🇺🇸

releases.title: Laying of the Time Capsule for the Ministry of Internal Affairs Center
releases.text:
Minister of Internal Affairs Ihor Klymenko, together with Protez Foundation President Yura Aroshidze, laid a time capsule in the foundation of Ukraine’s first Ministry of Internal Affairs Prosthetics and Orthotics Center.
        The facility is currently under reconstruction. Once completed, it will be equipped with state-of-the-art technology. The Center will become a space of support, recovery, and dignity for defenders with amputations.

releases.title: “L.P.S: Ukraine–USA”: 10 lyceum students of the Ministry of Internal Affairs went to the USA
releases.text:
10 lyceum students of the Ministry of Internal Affairs went to the USA as part of the educational trip “L.P.S: Ukraine-USA”.
        This is a unique opportunity for young Ukrainians to get acquainted with American culture, values, the security system and the work of the police, rescuers and military. And at the same time - to adequately present Ukrainian culture, strength of spirit and patriotism.
        The trip is organized in cooperation with the Prosthesis Foundation and the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine. We have been working on this project for more than four months to create a rich and valuable program for lyceum students.
